This miscellaneous appeal has been filed under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 being aggrieved with award dated 10.05.2023 passed by the Ist Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Narmadapuram in MACC No.27/2019 by which the claimant/respondent no.1 to 6 have been awarded Rs.36,19,909/- with interest @6%.

entities.text: Ist Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Narmadapuram
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2 . Facts giving rise to this appeal are that on 16.10.2016 at 9 pm the deceased-Kundan Lal was driving in the car MP-05-CA-3872.
The car driven and owned by respondent no.6.
By rash and negligent driving of the respondent no.6, the car overturned near Kehi Modh, Barkheda.
The deceased suffered the grievous injuries and he was admitted to Narmada Hospital, Hoshangabad where he was admitted since 16-22.10.2016.
When the injured situation became critical, he was admitted in Central India Institute of Medical Science, Nagpur where he was admitted for 22.10.2016 to 29.11.2016.

entities.text: Central India Institute of Medical Science, Nagpur
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: He was operated on 19.11.2016 and during treatment, the deceased Kundan Lal died on 19.05.2017.

The deceased was 44 years old and by farming earning Rs.3,00,000/- per annum and by the work of present Munim, he was earning Rs.10,000/- per month due to sudden death of deceased, the claimant has suffered loss of dependency.
3. The FIR was lodged in the police station Abdullahganj, Raisen.
The case was registered against respondent no.6.
After investigation, the charge sheet was filed against the respondent no.6.

4. Learned counsel for Insurance Company has submitted that the short point involved in the case is that the Claims Tribunal has wrongly calculated the Bills of treatment and he has argued that the Claims Tribunal has calculated the advance receipts for example from Ex.P-305 to P-330 in the expenditure and also added the provisional statement provided by the Hospital Ex.P-331 to P- 333 that were included in the Ex.P-334 and has also calculated the Bills of medicine that were issued on credit bills and were included in the final bill and also calculated the credit record summary Ex.P-185 in the expenditure.

Thus, the Claims Tribunal has triplicate the expenditure incurred by Royal Sundaram General Insurance Co. ... vs Smt. Aabha Sahu on 13 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/79967607/
2 the claimants while the deceased was hospitalised in CIIMS Hospital, Nagpur.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
He has also stated that this amount be corrected and he is not challenging the rest of the award.
5.

I have gone through the record and findings the material error while calculating the amount of expenditure and the Insurance has not challenged the award on other heads without hearing the other party.
The matter is decided in admission stage.

6. After excluding the receipts of advance and provisional statements from Ex.P-289, Ex.P-290,
Ex.P-305 to Ex.P-333, Ex.P-339 to Ex.P-342 and Ex.P-347 to Ex.P-349, the expenditure incurred in the treatments comes to Rs.10,64,449/-.
Thus, the amount of expenditure on treatment is reduced to Rs.11,36,388/-.
On the rest of the heads, the amount awarded by the Claims Tribunal is affirmed.

7. Thus, on the loss of dependency, for the consortium, loss of estate and funeral expenses, the amount decided by the Tribunal is kept intact and further amount of Rs.10,64,449/- is awarded in the head of expenditure of the treatment.
Total compensation amount comes to Rs.24,83,521/-.

Thus, the claimants are entitled an amount of Rs.24,83,521/- as a compensation and on that amount, they are also entitled for the simple interest @6% per annum from the date of application i.e. 05.02.2019 till the amount is deposited before the Claims Tribunal.
8.
The amount being deposited before Claims Tribunal, the Claims Tribunal shall disburse the amount in the same ratio.
With the same direction, as arrears in the para-49 of the award of the Claims Tribunal.
The parties shall bear their own cost.
9. With the copy of the order, the record of Claims Tribunal be returned back.
10. Record of the Claims Tribunal be consigned to the record room.

(DEVNARAYAN MISHRA) JUDGE HK Royal Sundaram General Insurance Co. ... vs Smt. Aabha Sahu on 13 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/79967607/
